### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A31 and A32 each appeared in 40 in 100 traces (80 of 200); in the later window, in about 53 in 100 (105 of 200). Each occurs at most once per trace in both windows, so the rise is in participation, not repetition. [OCC001, OCC002]
- In the earlier window, A33 and A34 each appeared in 60 in 100 traces (120 of 200); in the later window, in about 48 in 100 (95 of 200), likewise without repetition in either window. [OCC003, OCC004]
- The four shifts match in size (about 12–13 in 100 traces, two up and two down), and each difference is larger than about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- The event distance between A16 and A27 moved towards direct adjacency: distance 1 rose from about 41 to about 59 in 100 pair observations, while distance 2 fell from about 59 to about 41, on 88 observations before and 109 after. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, cases more often include A31 and A32 (from about 40 to about 53 in 100 traces each) and less often include A33 and A34 (from about 60 to about 48 in 100 each), all four by the same margin. This is consistent with the parts of the process containing A31/A32 being executed more often while the parts containing A33/A34 are executed less often; the mirrored, equal-sized shifts suggest a redistribution between two groups of route activities. Supporting signs: all four activities are observed in substantial shares in both windows, every item is unusual for random re-splits, and the identical figures within each pair suggest the paired activities move together. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

Across the whole comparison, 5 items qualified where roughly 0.27 would be expected by chance among the 55 tested units, so the set of differences as a whole is unlikely to be a sampling artefact. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, LAG001]

Limitation: the evidence contains no relational or direct-succession items for these four activities, so it cannot confirm that A31/A32 and A33/A34 are alternatives on two paths between which the shares shifted; the grouping rests on the mirrored pattern alone. An important competing explanation — four independent participation changes, such as individual activities becoming more or less often executed — cannot be ruled out. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

Other differences: the A16 → A27 pair now appears at event distance 1 in about 59 in 100 observations, up from about 41, a redistribution towards direct adjacency; on its own this does not show that an activity was moved, nor does it identify any step between them being skipped. [LAG001]
